full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.11.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Manikganj, passed in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2006 disallowing the appeal and affirming the judgment and order dated 26.06.2006 passed in the Title Suit No. 80 of 2005 by the learned Assistant Judge, Shingair, Manikganj rejecting the plaint, should not be set-aside. 

 2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit praying for cancellation of decree and partition of the suit land contending, inter-alia, that the 'Ka' schedule land was owned by Alam Sheikh and Munshi Sheikh and out of "Kha' scheduled land measuring 135 decimal Alam Sheikh, Bilokhonnesa and Munshi Sheikh were the owners of 45 decimal of land each. Munshi Sheikh died leaving behind 4(four) sons, namely Intaz, Chandu, Moizuddin, Ansu. Intaz died leaving behind 1 (one) son, namely, Polan Moizuddin died leaving behind 1 (one) son, namely Sheikh Gendu; Chandu sold 75 decimal of land of his share to Sheikh Polan and Sheikh Gendu vide deed no. 4798 dated 03.12.1973. Ansu died leaving behind 1 (one) son, namely, Aziz and 3(three) daughters. Aziz said his share to Sheikh Polan and Sheikh Gendu. Accordingly, Sheikh Gendu became the owner of 68.64 decimal of land form the scheduled properties by way of inheritance and purchase. Sheikh, Gendu and Sheikh Polan sold 15 decimals of land to Yasin. Gendu was owning and possessing 61.14 decimal of land and he died leaving 1(one) wife, namely, Koer Jaan, 6(six) sons, namely, Abbas Ali and others and 1 (one) daughter, namely Umair Jaan. Cherag Ali and others (heirs of Gendu) sold 37.5 decimal of land in 1993; accordingly, the heirs of Gendu are the owners of 23.64 decimal of lands. The daughter of Polan, namely, Meher Jaan has sold 8 decimal of land to plaintiff Abbas Ali, Mokib, Moksad and Saidur. Palau died leaving behind 1(one) wife, namely, Monura, 3(three) sons, namely, Afasuddin, Amizuddin and Hefazuddin and two daughters, namely, Mizjaan and Meher Jaan. Earlier a partition suit being numbered 14 of 2000 was filed by Afaz (Heir of Polan) where the heirs of Gendu were parties. In the said suit Afazuddin as plaintiff did not incorporate actual facts and obtained decree suppressing the existence of a deed being numbered 4798 dated 03.12.1973. Thereafter the plaintiff of the instant suit requested the said Afaz to give their legitimate shares of land in the light of the said deed; but Afaz adopted dilatory tactics as such the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the instant suit. 

 3. In the suit the defendants filed an application under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 08.11.2005. The learned Judge of the trial court after hearing the parties considering the materials on record and relevant provisions of law dismissed the suit by his judgment and order dated 26.02.2006. Against the said judgment and order the plaintiff preferred appeal before the learned District Judge, Manikganj. On transferred it was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge who after hearing the parties considering the materials on record dismissed the appeal affirmed the judgment and order of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 28.11.2006. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiffs as petitioners moved this court and obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr. Haroon Ar Rashid, the learned advocate appearing for the opposite-party No. 46 and 57 submits that both the courts below considering the materials on record and relevant provisions of law rightly found that the suit was barred by res-judicata under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and rightly passed judgment and decree. In support of his contention he has referred the decision reported in 10 MLR (AD) 90. 

 8. In order to appreciate the submissions made by the learned advocates for the parties, I have, gone through the revisional application, pleadings, judgment and decree of the courts below very carefully. 

 9. Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the court of appeal below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree. 

 10. On perusal of the record it appears that the petitioner as plaintiffs filed a Title Suit being No. 14 of 2000 where these defendants were parties in respect of same land which are admitted by the parties. The earlier suit was decreed in part. Against which defendant preferred appeal before the learned District Judge. On transferred it was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, First court who after hearing the parties and considering the materials on record allowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 24.11.2004. 

 15. In view of the discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I am of the view that impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this court in revision. Thus, I find no merit in the Rule.
